study: Hatswell & Porter 2018, Appl Health Econ Health Policy 17
verification_level: Crossref metadata + title only (abstract not retrievable; publisher page bot-blocked)
objective: Reduce drug wastage for weight/BSA-dosed drugs (per title)
user_choice: Dispensing rule: whole vials covering dose
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: Identical structure: choose discrete unit sizes so that whole-unit covering of a stochastic continuous requirement minimises expected leftover; FUGD under rational choice is this problem with sheet area in place of dose
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: Different product domain only; no new mathematics

study: Matsuo et al. 2020, BMC Health Serv Res 20
objective: Reduce discarded residual drug and cost
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: Expected overage = E[unit·ceil(R/unit) − R] evaluated on measured requirements
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: Shows the domain where this problem is already empirically evaluated; FUGD lacks the corresponding requirement data

user_choice: Larger size substitutes for smaller (downward substitution)
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: FUGD with selectable single units (no combination) and 'use the smallest unit that covers the task' is a one-dimensional assortment problem with scrap-type substitution cost = material overage
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: Material overage as substitution cost is already Pentico's 'scrap' cost case (Pentico 1976)

user_choice: Unit larger on both dimensions substitutes
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: FUGD with width-and-length tasks (continuous width w_t, length l_t) maps to the discrete two-dimensional assortment problem
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: None mathematically; width×length partition grid is a structured special case

user_choice: Choice model with size tolerance (half-size up/down)
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: Stochastic/tolerant user choice over unit sizes = size-substitution choice model; FUGD's 'stochastic choice' variant is covered
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: Material-per-success objective instead of revenue is an objective substitution, not a new class

study: Jacques & Alexandridis 2019, Appl Sci 9 (tablet scoring review)
design_variables: Score lines / partition of a solid unit
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: Direct physical analogue: a manufactured unit with user-breakable partition lines to select a fraction; perforation of a sheet is the same design idea
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: FUGD would add nothing conceptually; tissue domain transfer only

user_choice: Unit bias: people take a unit count, so amount scales with unit size
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: Habitual/count-based choice model of FUGD = unit-bias model; prediction 'smaller units reduce consumption' already demonstrated for food
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: Testing unit bias for tissue would be an empirical replication in a new domain; requires human-subject data this project does not have

mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: Package (unit) size choice under consumption heterogeneity and waste; includes the result that smaller packages are optimal under linear/convex cost
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: FUGD's 'finer is better unless other cost' observation is analogous

study: van Hove 2001, J Money Credit Banking 33; van Hove & Heyndels 1996 EJOR 90
objective: Min number of pieces exchanged (principle of least effort)
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: Combination-allowed FUGD (take several units to reach a requirement) is the denomination problem; handling effort vs overage trade-off is the classical least-effort criterion
Supplies the manufacturing-feasibility side; does not optimise granularity
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: Could parameterise a strength constraint, but no data on centre/longitudinal perforation

user_choice: Product variants matched to user need
mathematical_overlap_with_FUGD: Same 'match the unit to the need' idea evaluated by LCA for consumables
possible_additional_contribution_of_FUGD: FUGD would be an LCA-free sizing heuristic; not novel as a design principle
